placement._note: The customer places the microscope with a ruler: the centre of its plate holder this far beyond the platform's long edge nearest the rotation module (+y) and this far from the platform's left end (the end with the arm pillar). 340 mm from j1 keeps the wrist 60 mm inside the 400 mm reach, so the camera can be taken 40 mm ahead (bringup/sections.py TAG_AHEAD_MM) to see the plate's tag; a seat at 399 mm cannot (tried 2026-10-28).

Heights above the tool point for the arm's links (the CAD gives them once k is fixed).

reading_in_robot_frame._note: 'base' read as the base box's right edge, j1 (robot x 126) 60 mm beyond it. Then: base box x -84..66, slot line x 316, hotel end x 556, platform x -84..566. The slot line at 316 agrees with the module seat (317), the operator's 'aligned with column A'; the taught-pose hotel x (293, plate centre) is 23 mm off it. [Superseded by 'cad': the taught poses are wrist poses, the plate sits 205 mm ahead of them.]

cad._note: From the manufacturer's STEP assembly (Polar R400 Z400, SolidWorks 2020; the file itself is not in the repo). CAD frame: x across the platform, y UP, z along the platform's long side. Mapping to the robot frame, fixed by the j1 axis (CAD x 0, z -102.1 = robot 126, 0): robot x = cad z + 228.1, robot y = cad x, robot z = cad y + k. It is right-handed. k is not fixed by the file (the CAD arm is stowed at an unknown column height); one touch of the finger bottom on the platform top fixes it.

mapping.note: CAD (x_c, z_c) -> robot plane: robot = R(theta) m(c) + t with m(c) = (z_c, x_c). With theta = 0 and t = j1_robot - m(j1_cad) this is x_r = z_c + 228.1, y_r = x_c. python bringup/register.py's register() finds theta and t from the arm's own observations; z_r = y_c + k.
